newsitem.title: INDIA: India revises up 95/96 cotton output estimates.
newsitem.headline: India revises up 95/96 cotton output estimates.

text.p: India's Cotton Advisory Board (CAB) has revised up its estimate of cotton output for 1995/96 (Sept-Aug) to a record 15.6 million bales from 14.9 million previously, a top industry official said on Wednesday.
One bale equals 170 kg (375 pounds) of cotton.
"The increase in production this year would be due to the increase in area under cotton cultivation," M.P. Gajaria, Indian Cotton Mills Federation (ICMF) chairman, told Reuters.
Analysts said India's widespread monsoon rains had set India on track for a bumper cotton crop for the third season in a row. The new crop was expected in another 10 days.
CAB, which consists of members of cotton trade associations, mill owners and government officials, decided on the fresh output figures after its meeting in Bombay on Monday.
Gajaria said the area under cotton cultivation in 1995/96 had increased to 8.96 million hectares from 7.86 million in 1994/95.
"But the yield per hectare of nearly 300 kgs this year compared to last year is more or less the same," Gajaria said.
In 1994/95 India produced 13.85 million bales of cotton.
"The crop year has been revised to meet the long pending demand of the cotton industry."
Gajaria said the government in 1995/96 had allowed export of 1.49 million bales of which only 800,000 bales had been shipped by the end of August.
Until last year, India allowed a maximum of 500,000 bales of cotton exports as part of government policy.
Despite this year's bumper crop, mill owners fear there will be little left over for export after domestic requirements have been satisfied.
India might not be able to meet this year's export target as the domestic requirement of cotton was expected to be around 14.8 million bales in 1995/96, Gajaria said.
In 1994/95 India exported only 108,000 bales of cotton.
"The exports this year compared to last year grew by leaps and bounds," Gajaria said. "This was because Indian cotton prices were relatively easier compared to prices of other countries."
CAB has also revised the cotton crop year from September-August to October-November.
"There is hardly any movement of cotton in the month of September. The real movement of Cotton starts from November onwards," Gajaria said.
